text:
Jade: rolling upgrade of chart 'redis-gpu' hit a bad state in prod-eu, helm returned non-zero and rollback hung :grimacing:
Omar: link the deploy? which release name?
Jade: release redis-gpu.prod-eu, running helm v3.9.1 via our release pipeline. deploy-bot shows pre-upgrade job created ok then stuck creating a job in namespace 'model-serving' which is Terminating
infra-bot: namespace model-serving is PendingDelete due to ResourceQuota controller blocking namespace garbage collection (quota ttl ttl-controller-policy=30m reached)
Maria: I see ResourceQuota 'compute-quota' shows used>hard because we had a burst of GPU pods earlier, new job couldn't schedule, but why is namespace stuck Terminating?
Ken: often Terminating namespaces have finalizers on PVCs or CRDs. run: kubectl get namespace model-serving -o json | jq .spec.finalizers
Jade: ran that, shows ["kubernetes"] actually, but pods show status Terminating and a stuck PVC with finalizer kubernetes.io/pvc-protection
Omar: paste logs of the hook pod?
Jade: ```bash
kubectl get pods -n model-serving
NAME                                  READY   STATUS        RESTARTS   AGE
pre-upgrade-job-abc123                 0/1     Terminating   0          6m
gpu-worker-0                           0/1     Terminating   2          2h
```
Maria: helm rollback waited on hook delete but since namespace GC blocked, rollback can't recreate resources -> pipeline times out and leaves release in FAILED state
Ken: this is nasty because the chart is multi-namespace and our rollback logic is namespace-scoped; ArgoCD/Flux will also see drift and refuse sync until namespace is healthy
Jade: immediate mitigation idea: remove pvc-protection finalizer on the orphan PVCs, let namespace finish terminating, then rerun rollback (or force-uninstall the release). Thoughts?
Omar: +1 but need audit trail. Create ticket and note approvals. Also check ResourceQuota TTL policy - why did quota controller set TTL? recent change in infra CI?
infra-bot: recent change merged: terraform:namespace_policy->enable_quota_ttl = true (PR #4823) applied 2h before incident
Maria: that explains it. Quota TTL removed orphaned quota objects but left namespace in a state where GC waits on resource deletion but can't proceed due to PVC finalizers
Ken: plan:
- step 1: patch PVC finalizer to remove protection (kubectl patch pvc <name> -n model-serving -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' --type=merge)
- step 2: kubectl delete namespace model-serving --grace-period=0 --force
- step 3: rerun helm rollback from pipeline with --force (helm rollback redis-gpu <prev> --namespace model-serving)
- step 4: revert terraform flag enable_quota_ttl in staging and run canary in a dev cluster
Jade: executing step1 now (will record commands in INFRA-1234)
Omar: ping infra-sre for a quick thumbs-up before force-delete. tagging @Ken for runbook sign-off
Ken: signed off. ensure we capture kube-apiserver audit logs and attach to ticket.
Jade: done patching, PVC removed finalizers, namespace terminating cleared within ~40s
deploy-bot: detected namespace recreation, requeued helm rollback job in pipeline
Maria: re-run succeeded, release back to v12 and pods coming up, GPU quotas slowly decreasing as old pods terminate
Omar: follow-ups: revert quota TTL flag, add a pipeline pre-check for namespace health (no Terminating namespaces, no PendingResourceQuota issues), and add better rollback path that can target cluster-scoped objects first
Jade: creating INFRA-1234 with action items, will include remediation commands and timeline. thanks team :thumbsup:
Ken: adding postmortem label and scheduling 30m blameless review tomorrow
